findings.message: Instance fix, and the same defect is still open. This round again changed only the tool description (mcp-utilisation.ts:10) and the README. Both now document the gap instead of closing it. `people` is still built only from `mine.status` and `team.rows`, and both need a `time.week` row. Anyone who logged nothing that week is left out, including the viewer. So `below` can never return the person who is furthest below target. The description tells chat that a missing person 'either has no timesheet that week or isn't someone you may see', which still treats 'logged nothing' and 'not visible' as one answer. Fix: list every person the viewer may see. Use the same 071 scope that `teamWeek`/`seesWeek` apply, over hr people, plus the viewer. Show anyone without a week at 0 h with status null, against their target, with every working day before today in `missingDays`. Add a variant test: the viewer with no week, a report with no week, and a PM-visible person with no week.
findings.scenario: Maya calls get_week_utilisation { week: '2026-W43', below: 80 } while Dinesh, her report, has logged nothing in W43 (no time.week row). Expected: Dinesh at 0 h, 0%, with all past weekdays missing. Actual: he is absent, and chat answers that he 'has no timesheet or isn't someone you may see'.

findings.message: The round-3 fix now also counts `hoursIncomplete` rows in `team.leftOut`. Two places that explain `leftOut` still give only the old reason. The lede at view.ts:44 says '... left out of the team figure: their leave isn't visible to you', and the contract doc at contracts.ts:26 says '`leftOut` had leave the viewer can't see'. A person left out because their timesheet status is unknown is therefore explained as hidden leave. Fix: count the two reasons apart (for example `leftOut` and `statusUnknown`, or a per-reason breakdown), give the matching sentence in the lede and the CSV/Team row, and update the contract doc.
findings.scenario: Maya can see Dinesh's leave, and Dinesh has a copied hour whose week Time no longer holds. get_utilisation returns team.leftOut = 1, and the lede reads '1 person is left out of the team figure: their leave isn't visible to you.' That reason is false: his leave is visible and his timesheet status is what's unknown.

findings.message: The 'status unknown → incomplete' fix (inputs.ts unknownFor) is proven by one case, and that case plants an orphan `week_id` by hand in `reports.logged_hours`. The fix covers two variants that real paths can reach, and neither is tested. (1) Time switched off (`hasModule('time', …)` false): set `setInstalledModules` without 'time' on a database whose copied hours carry week ids that have no status row. Every such person must come back `hoursIncomplete`, not dropped. (2) A week the viewer may not see in Time while the copied hour is still visible, or a week removed through Time's own retention or erasure path. Fix: make this a table-driven test with at least the Time-off case and one more case driven through a real path, beside the planted one.
findings.scenario: Revert the `unknownFor` marking so that rows with no status are dropped silently whenever `hasModule('time')` is false. The suite stays green, because the only test plants a week id that Time lacks while Time is installed.
